drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank CCKP provides UAE-specific extreme-precipitation projections for 2025, 2050, 2075 and 2085. KPI: maximum 1-day precipitation; flood-zone exposure; drainage capacity; downtime; repair costs.

drivers.name: Urban Heat Island
drivers.logic: Dense urban development can amplify heat exposure and increase cooling requirements, particularly in highly built-up areas.
drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank's UAE heat-risk methodology explicitly identifies urban heat-island effects as exacerbating heat risks. KPI: urban-rural temperature differential; cooling kWh/m²; green-space coverage; surface temperature.
drivers.keySources: World Bank – UAE Compounded Heat Risks

drivers.name: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure
drivers.logic: Heat, flooding, water stress and coastal risks can disrupt critical utilities and transport infrastructure, making resilience investment material for large developments.
drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank climate-risk datasets provide UAE-specific exposure information for heat, extreme precipitation and coastal flooding. KPI: % critical infrastructure covered by resilience plans; adaptation capex; service-interruption hours; assets exposed.
drivers.keySources: World Bank – UAE Climate Knowledge Portal

drivers.name: Low-Carbon Cement & Steel
drivers.logic: Cement and steel are major embodied-carbon sources in real estate. UAE industrial decarbonisation targets increasingly affect the carbon intensity and availability of construction materials.
drivers.evidenceKpi: UAE Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap targets 5% industrial-emissions reduction by 2030, 63% by 2040 and 93% by 2050, covering cement, iron, steel and aluminium. KPI: kgCO₂e/m²; low-carbon material %; EPD coverage.
drivers.keySources: UAE Ministry of Industry – Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap

drivers.name: Low-Carbon Material Procurement
drivers.logic: UAE policy is explicitly encouraging demand for lower-carbon construction materials, increasing the relevance of procurement specifications and supplier selection for developers.
drivers.evidenceKpi: UAE Green Business Toolkit recommends creating demand for low-carbon steel through procurement and design specifications and increasing use of recycled scrap and low-carbon technologies. KPI: % low-carbon steel/cement; recycled content; supplier emissions.

drivers.name: Sustainable / Certified Materials
drivers.logic: Al Sa'fat and other green-building requirements increase demand for materials meeting specified environmental and technical performance criteria.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Dubai Municipality's factory-assessment framework includes standards for cement, slag cement, GGBS, steel structures, insulation and other construction products, including products relevant to Al Sa'fat. KPI: % compliant materials; recycled content; certified suppliers.

drivers.name: Construction Waste & Circularity
drivers.logic: Large development activity creates material waste and increases the value of reuse, recycling and resource-efficient procurement.
drivers.evidenceKpi: UAE green-construction policy promotes resource efficiency and circular approaches; cement/steel guidance specifically encourages use of residual waste, by-products and recycled scrap. KPI: kg waste/m²; recycling/reuse %; landfill diversion; recycled-content %.

drivers.name: Supplier ESG / Responsible Procurement
drivers.logic: Green-building requirements and institutional investment increasingly require developers to demonstrate that contractors and material suppliers meet environmental and technical standards.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Dubai Municipality maintains formal conformity/factory-assessment requirements covering major construction products. KPI: % suppliers screened; ESG clauses; certified suppliers; supplier incidents.

drivers.name: Construction-Material Decarbonisation
drivers.logic: The UAE's industrial decarbonisation pathway will increasingly affect the carbon intensity, technology mix and procurement requirements of construction-material suppliers.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Industrial roadmap covers cement, iron, steel and aluminium and targets cumulative industrial CO₂ reductions of 2.9 Gt by 2050. KPI: supplier tCO₂e/t product; Scope 1–2 emissions; low-carbon product share.
drivers.keySources: UAE Ministry of Industry – Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap

drivers.name: Saudi Building Code – Energy Conservation (SBC 601/602)
drivers.logic: Mandatory energy-conservation provisions directly affect building envelope, HVAC, ventilation, lighting and hot-water design.
drivers.evidenceKpi: SBC 601–602 specify minimum energy-efficiency requirements covering exterior envelope, HVAC/ventilation, lighting and service-water heating. KPI: kWh/m²; envelope U-value; HVAC efficiency; compliance rate.
drivers.keySources: Saudi Building Code – Code System (Saudi Business Council)

drivers.name: Saudi Green Building Code (SBC 1001)
drivers.logic: Establishes sustainability requirements covering energy, water, materials, waste, site development and indoor environmental quality, making resource efficiency a development consideration.
drivers.evidenceKpi: SBC 1001 explicitly covers energy conservation, CO₂ reduction, water conservation, resource efficiency and material-waste recycling, and provides for green-building classification. KPI: energy/water intensity; CO₂; recycled content; waste recycling %.
drivers.keySources: Saudi Building Code – SBC 1001 (Saudi Business Council)

drivers.name: Saudi Net Zero 2060 / NDC
drivers.logic: National decarbonisation commitments increase long-term transition pressure on buildings and real-estate assets, particularly through energy efficiency and lower-carbon development.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia targets net zero by 2060 and its NDC targets reducing/removing/avoiding 278 MtCO₂e annually by 2030. KPI: kgCO₂e/m²; operational emissions; renewable-energy share.
drivers.keySources: UNFCCC – Saudi Arabia Updated NDC (UNFCCC); PIF Green Finance Framework (Public Investment Fund)

drivers.name: REGA Comprehensive Real Estate Strategy
drivers.logic: Saudi Arabia's real-estate strategy explicitly includes sector sustainability and procedures to ensure the sustainability of real-estate assets, strengthening ESG relevance across development and asset management.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Strategy has 4 pillars, including “Empowerment and Sustainability”; explicitly calls for procedures to ensure sustainability of real-estate assets. KPI: sustainable assets; sustainability procedures; ESG compliance.

drivers.name: Housing Development / Homeownership Target
drivers.logic: Government-supported housing development creates sustained demand for residential construction and financing, increasing the scale at which energy and resource-efficiency requirements apply.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi homeownership reached 66.24% in 2025, against a 70% 2030 target. KPI: housing units delivered; homeownership; development pipeline; energy performance of new housing.

drivers.name: Green Finance for Real Estate & Infrastructure
drivers.logic: Saudi sustainable-finance frameworks create a dedicated financing channel for eligible green projects, including energy efficiency, sustainable water and other environmental infrastructure relevant to real estate.
drivers.evidenceKpi: PIF Green Finance Framework permits issuance of green bonds, sukuk and loans for eligible green projects; eligible categories include energy efficiency and sustainable water management.
drivers.keySources: PIF – Green Finance Framework (Public Investment Fund)

drivers.name: Green Bonds
drivers.logic: Rapid development of Saudi green-debt markets provides an increasingly established source of climate-linked capital for large-scale sustainable development.
drivers.evidenceKpi: PIF's €1.65bn green bond issued in October 2025 was >6× oversubscribed, with orders exceeding €10bn. Proceeds are allocated to eligible green projects including energy efficiency and sustainable water.

drivers.name: Green / Sustainable Sukuk Market
drivers.logic: Sukuk is a significant source of debt capital in Saudi Arabia and increasingly has a sustainable-finance component relevant to infrastructure and real-estate development.
drivers.evidenceKpi: PIF issued US$1.5bn sukuk in 2024 and its green bond was increased from US$1.25bn to US$1.75bn; both transactions were 5× oversubscribed.
drivers.keySources: PIF – Green Bond & Sukuk, 2024 (Public Investment Fund)

drivers.name: Sustainable Debt Market Regulation
drivers.logic: Saudi capital-market regulation is formalising green, social, sustainable and sustainability-linked debt, making environmental performance increasingly relevant to issuers seeking labelled financing.
drivers.evidenceKpi: CMA's guidelines for Green, Social, Sustainable and Sustainability-Linked Debt Instruments became effective 27 May 2025 and require environmental/social benefits to be assessed and, where feasible, quantified.
drivers.keySources: CMA – Green, Social & Sustainability Guidelines (هيئة السوق المالية)

drivers.name: Sukuk / Debt Financing for Real Estate Funds
drivers.logic: Development of the sukuk and debt market creates additional financing channels for real-estate investment vehicles and developers.
drivers.evidenceKpi: CMA's 2024–2026 strategy explicitly includes regulatory development for sukuk/debt instruments issued by closed-end real-estate traded funds.

drivers.name: Energy-Efficiency Investment
drivers.logic: Saudi Arabia's hot climate and building-energy requirements create a material investment opportunity in efficient HVAC, building envelopes, controls and retrofits.
drivers.evidenceKpi: SBC 601/602 explicitly covers HVAC, ventilation, lighting, service-water heating and building envelope efficiency. KPI: kWh/m² savings; retrofit capex; payback; HVAC efficiency.

drivers.name: Large-Scale Real Estate Investment Pipeline
drivers.logic: Saudi housing and urban-development programmes create substantial demand for development capital; this increases the potential market for green financing where projects satisfy eligibility requirements.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Homeownership reached 66.24% in 2025, with a 70% target by 2030. PIF's domestic investments exceeded US$199bn cumulatively since 2021 and its AUM exceeded US$900bn in 2025.
drivers.keySources: Vision 2030 – 2025 Annual Report (Saudi Vision 2030); PIF 2025 Annual Report announcement (Public Investment Fund)

drivers.name: Extreme Heat
drivers.logic: Extreme heat increases cooling demand, affects occupant comfort and creates health/productivity risks for construction workers.
drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank projects a substantial increase in extreme heat exposure; Saudi Arabia's average annual temperature has already increased by approximately 2°C since 1960. KPI: cooling-degree days; days >40°C; peak cooling load; kWh/m².
drivers.keySources: World Bank – Saudi Arabia Climate Risk Country Profile (worldbank.org)

drivers.name: Water Scarcity
drivers.logic: Severe water scarcity makes efficient water use, resilient supply and water recycling material to real-estate operating costs and asset resilience.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia has <100 m³ renewable freshwater resources per capita/year, placing it in the category of absolute water scarcity. KPI: m³/m²; potable-water intensity; recycled-water %; water-stress exposure.

drivers.name: Flash Flooding / Extreme Rainfall
drivers.logic: Short-duration intense rainfall can cause flash floods that damage buildings, roads, drainage systems and other urban infrastructure.
drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank identifies flooding as a significant climate hazard for Saudi Arabia, with intense rainfall events creating urban and infrastructure exposure. KPI: flood-exposed assets; drainage capacity; downtime; repair cost; expected annual loss.
drivers.keySources: World Bank – Saudi Arabia Climate Risk Country Profile

drivers.name: Sea-Level Rise / Coastal Flooding
drivers.logic: Coastal real-estate development faces long-term exposure to sea-level rise, coastal flooding and saltwater impacts on infrastructure.
drivers.evidenceKpi: World Bank climate projections provide Saudi-specific sea-level-rise and coastal-flooding exposure projections. KPI: % assets in coastal/flood zones; projected sea-level rise; expected annual loss; adaptation capex.
drivers.keySources: World Bank – Saudi Arabia Climate Change Knowledge Portal

drivers.name: Dust & Sandstorms
drivers.logic: Dust and sandstorms can reduce outdoor air quality, increase HVAC filtration and maintenance requirements and disrupt construction activities.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia experiences frequent dust and sandstorm events, with dust exposure identified as an environmental/health risk. KPI: dust-event days; PM10/PM2.5; HVAC maintenance cost; construction downtime.

drivers.name: Urban Heat Island
drivers.logic: Dense urbanisation and extensive hard surfaces can amplify heat exposure and increase cooling demand in major Saudi cities.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi urban development is concentrated in major cities where built-up density can amplify local heat exposure. KPI: urban-rural temperature differential; cooling kWh/m²; surface temperature; green-space ratio.

drivers.name: Climate-Resilient Mega-Projects
drivers.logic: The long asset lives and scale of Saudi mega-projects increase the financial significance of physical climate-risk screening, resilience design and adaptation investment.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia's PIF has >SAR 3tn assets under management and is developing large-scale urban/infrastructure projects with multi-decade asset lives. KPI: % assets climate-screened; adaptation capex; expected annual loss; resilience coverage.

drivers.name: Low-Carbon Cement & Steel
drivers.logic: Saudi Arabia's construction pipeline creates significant embodied-carbon exposure through cement, steel and aluminium, making supplier carbon intensity increasingly material.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia is targeting 278 MtCO₂e of annual emissions reductions/avoidance by 2030, while its industrial decarbonisation programme covers cement, steel and other energy-intensive materials. KPI: kgCO₂e/m²; kgCO₂e/t material; low-carbon material %.
drivers.keySources: Saudi Ministry of Industry – Industrial Strategy; UNFCCC – Saudi NDC

drivers.name: Local Construction-Material Supply
drivers.logic: Localisation of construction-material production can reduce import/logistics exposure and strengthen supply-chain resilience for the country's large development pipeline.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia's National Industrial Development and Logistics Program targets localisation of industrial value chains and increased domestic manufacturing. KPI: local-content %; domestic procurement %; import dependency; supplier concentration.

drivers.name: Construction Waste & Circularity
drivers.logic: Large-scale construction increases material consumption and waste, creating opportunities to reduce disposal costs and embodied emissions through reuse, recycling and circular procurement.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Arabia's National Waste Management Center regulates waste management and has established national targets/frameworks for waste diversion and recycling. KPI: kg waste/m²; recycling %; reuse %; landfill diversion.
drivers.keySources: Saudi National Center for Waste Management

drivers.name: Supplier ESG / Responsible Procurement
drivers.logic: Large Saudi developers and PIF-backed projects increasingly need supplier governance covering environmental, social, labour, health and safety performance.
drivers.evidenceKpi: PIF's ESG framework incorporates ESG considerations into its investment approach and portfolio-company expectations. KPI: % suppliers screened; ESG clauses; H&S incidents; supplier audit coverage.

drivers.name: Supply-Chain Emissions / Embodied Carbon
drivers.logic: Developers need primary supplier data on cement, steel, aluminium, glass and other materials to quantify embodied carbon and manage Scope 3 emissions.
drivers.evidenceKpi: GHG Protocol Category 1 – Purchased Goods and Services covers upstream emissions from purchased construction materials. KPI: Scope 3 Cat. 1 tCO₂e; kgCO₂e/m²; supplier-data coverage; % primary emissions data.

drivers.name: Climate-Resilient Construction Materials
drivers.logic: Extreme heat, dust, water scarcity and coastal exposure increase the importance of material durability and performance under Saudi climatic conditions.
drivers.evidenceKpi: Saudi Building Code includes requirements affecting building envelope, thermal performance, moisture and material/building-system performance. KPI: material service life; replacement cycle; thermal performance; maintenance cost.
